head: 5654d9b2979db5964482574059927f0595467ba1
summary:
The fix holds against everything this machine could reach. The acceptance command exits 0: 1 run through eng/dotnet.ps1 and 10 of 10 more idle runs. The committed acceptance tests still catch the bug: run against the pre-fix guard in a scratch copy, they are red 3 of 3 with 'interrupted 1 time(s), 1 cancel attempt(s) made'.

The machine rules limit load to half the logical CPUs, so the design's 32 busy jobs were not allowed. 8 unpinned busy loops did not reproduce the flake on the unfixed guard (12 of 12 green), so that load cannot tell fixed from unfixed. Instead I confined the contention to 2 CPUs: the test process plus 4 Normal-priority spinners, all pinned to CPUs 14 and 15. Under that load the unfixed guard was red 13 of 13 on CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel, always 'still blocked 2 s after Cancel, interrupted 1 time(s)'. The fixed tree passed that test 30 of 30, and both repro tests 30 of 30.

The fixed class runs were red 2 of 30, both on the pre-existing 250 ms 'Cancel() took N ms' bar in CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel (355 and 717 ms). The unfixed baseline also went red on that bar (1 of 6), and the build had already recorded it as a separate defect. The full suite, 301 tests, passed 10 of 10 idle and 8 of 8 under 8 busy loops.

O-002, O-003 and O-004 were verified directly. A scratch copy of the guard recorded when each CancelSynchronousIo was called and returned, alongside the worker's waits, in 13 idle and 6 contended traces. Every time the worker blocked again, the previous attempt was still held in the kernel, and it returned only after the next attempt, on another thread, had cancelled the new wait. That held for 2 of 2 re-blocks at 3 waits and 7 of 7 at 8 waits, in every trace. Every attempt returned before Exit did, no attempt was issued after Exit began, and the wait after Exit was never aborted.

Scratch probes also confirmed three behaviours no test in the tree pins:
- The cap: with every attempt held for 1 s, at most 4 were live and 4 were made (7 of 7).
- A failed Thread.Start gives its slot back, and a later tick delivers the cancel (7 of 7).
- Dispose waits for an attempt still in flight before closing the handle. With that wait removed, the handle closed first and the attempt then hit the closed handle, which the guard caught (3 of 3).

The republished app passed WindowCases C-006: Stop pressed mid-scan, and the scan returned 9 ms after Cancel. All 49 fitness rules hold.

Still open:
- O-026 and O-027, the two test fixes code review asked for, are owed to build-slice and not in the tree. HEAD is still 5654d9b.
- The acceptance test's 2 s bar has thin margin under concentrated contention: one run printed 2051 ms, measured after the wait had already returned in time.

checks.what: Acceptance command exactly as the engine phrases it
checks.evidence: EXIT 0, 2 of 2 passed. 3 waits: left 69 ms after Cancel, interrupted 3, 3 attempts, 3 delivered, at most 2 live, 2 live at Exit. 8 waits: 219 ms, interrupted 8, 8 delivered, at most 2 live.

checks.what: Acceptance tests repeated idle
checks.evidence: 0 of 10 red. 3 waits left 136-285 ms after Cancel; 8 waits 196-225 ms; peak 2 live every run.

checks.what: The committed acceptance tests still detect the bug (pre-fix guard from 1922131 plus inert stubs for PeakAttemptsInKernel, AttemptsLiveAtLastDrain and BeforeCancelCall, in a %TEMP% copy)
checks.evidence: Red 3 of 3, as expected: 'the call was still blocked 2 s after Cancel, interrupted 1 time(s), 1 cancel attempt(s) made' and '...10 s after Cancel, interrupted 1 time(s), 1 cancel attempt(s) made'.

checks.what: Baseline: unfixed guard class under 8 unpinned busy loops (half of 16 logical CPUs, the most the machine rules allow)
checks.command: loop.ps1 -Mode spread8 -Filter FullyQualifiedName~SynchronousIoCancelTests on the unfixed copy (x12)
checks.evidence: This load did not reproduce the flake: CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel passed 12 of 12 on the unfixed guard. Every run was red only on ExitWaitsForAttemptsAboutToCancelSoNoneLandsAfterIt, a new test the old guard cannot pass. So spread8 cannot tell fixed from unfixed. 8 busy processes were stopped, 0 left.

checks.what: Baseline: unfixed flaky test under contention confined to 2 CPUs (the test process and 4 Normal-priority spinners pinned to CPUs 14 and 15)
checks.command: loop.ps1 -Mode pinned2 on the unfixed csproj, --filter ...CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel (5-minute budget, 7 runs)
checks.evidence: Red 7 of 7 with 'the call was still blocked 2 s after Cancel, interrupted 1 time(s)', the reported flake signature. This load discriminates. Busy processes stopped, 0 left.

checks.what: Baseline: unfixed guard class through the test dll under pinned2 (the new-guard-only tests excluded)
checks.command: loop.ps1 -Mode pinned2 on the unfixed dll, filter SynchronousIoCancelTests minus ExitWaits and DisposeWithoutExit (6 runs)
checks.evidence: The flake was red 6 of 6 ('still blocked 2 s after Cancel, interrupted 1 time(s)'). CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel was red 1 of 6 with 'Cancel() took 464 ms' on its 250 ms bar, so that bar goes red under this load before the fix too.

checks.what: Fixed tree: the reported flaky test under pinned2, 30 runs
checks.command: loop.ps1 -Mode pinned2 -Proj <tree>\tests\FsAnalyser.Core.Tests\bin\Debug\net10.0-windows\FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.dll -Filter FullyQualifiedName~SynchronousIoCancel (5 passes, 30 runs, blame-hang 60 s)
checks.evidence: 30 trx files, 900 results. CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel passed 30 of 30 (max test duration 2503 ms, 200 ms settle included). CancelFreesACallThatBlocksAgainBeforeTheCancelCallHasReturned passed 30 of 30; its printed Cancel-to-leave was 317-2051 ms (bar 2 s; the clock is read after left.Wait returns). CancelFreesACallThatBlocksAgainMoreTimesThanTheCapOfLiveAttempts passed 30 of 30 (706-5088 ms, bar 10 s). Peak live 2 or 3, never 4. No hang dumps.

checks.what: Fixed tree: every run of both guard classes green under pinned2
checks.evidence: 28 of 30 green. 2 red runs, both CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel on its 250 ms PromptCancel bar: 'Cancel() took 355 ms' and 'Cancel() took 717 ms'. That test asserts its 2 s Join first, so the Join passed in both. The bar is also red in the unfixed baseline (1 of 6), and StartCanceller, the code under Cancel(), did not change. The build recorded this as a separate defect; whether it belongs to SL-055 is a design question no person has answered.

checks.what: Full suite with the repro included, idle
checks.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx -nologo [--no-build] --blame-hang-timeout 60s (1 build run, 1 diagnostic run, then x8)
checks.evidence: 10 of 10 green, 301 passed and 0 failed each time, about 21-23 s of test time.

checks.what: Full suite under 8 unpinned busy loops
checks.command: loop.ps1 -Mode spread8 -Proj FsAnalyser.slnx -Filter '' (x8, no --filter, so the csproj's default trait filter applies)
checks.evidence: 8 of 8 exit 0. Repro 3 waits 56-74 ms, 8 waits 198-236 ms, peak 2. 8 busy processes stopped, 0 left.

checks.what: Instrumented trace of attempt calls and returns against the worker's waits, one CPU, worker at Highest (scratch copy only)
checks.command: ValidateScratchTests.TraceOneCpu(3|8), 1+6 idle runs and 6 pinned2 runs, checked by checktrace.ps1
checks.evidence: In every trace, each attempt k was still inside CancelSynchronousIo after the worker entered wait k+1 (2 of 2 at 3 waits, 7 of 7 at 8 waits). It returned TRUE only after attempt k+1's call had freed wait k+1. Example: csio-call 1 at 222.66 ms, wait-enter 2 at 223.37, csio-call 2 at 250.10, wait-left 2 at 250.16, csio-ret-TRUE 1 at 250.26. Calls always equalled returns; 0 calls after the final Leave; 0 returns after exit-returned; the post-Exit pending wait was never aborted. Cancel to Exit: idle 122-207 ms, pinned2 965-2326 ms.

checks.what: Cap probe: every attempt held before its call for 1 s (40 ticks), then released (scratch)
checks.evidence: 7 of 7: 'held for 1 s: peak 4, attempts 4; after release: peak 4, attempts 4, delivered 4, live at drain 0'. The worker was freed and Exit returned.

checks.what: Thread.Start failure injection: the first two dispatches throw OutOfMemoryException (scratch-only VFailStart seam)
checks.evidence: 7 of 7: 2 injected start failures, then attempt 1 delivered; peak 1 (the failed starts leaked no slot); live at drain 0. Freed 85 ms after Cancel idle, 475-620 ms under pinned2.

checks.what: Dispose without Exit while an attempt is in flight (held 150 ms before its call), with a skip-drain mutant switch (scratch)
checks.evidence: Drain on: 3 of 3 pass, liveAtLastDrain=1; csio-call 2 at 180.90, csio-ret-FALSE 2 at 180.91, handle-closing at 180.95. Skip-drain mutant: 3 of 3 red; the handle closed at about 56 ms, and attempt 2 then hit ObjectDisposedException at about 181 ms (caught by CancelOnce). So Dispose really does wait, and a test of this shape has teeth.

checks.what: Architecture rules
checks.evidence: 49 rules checked against 83 files; every declared rule holds, including 'Cancel attempts never run on the thread pool or a timer'.

checks.what: Published app: Stop pressed mid-scan
checks.evidence: PASSED, EXIT 0 in 53 s. artifacts/publish/FsAnalyser.App.exe was republished at 13:05, after the guard's last change. Stopped after 750 of 30150 folders; 'the scan returned within 2 s of Cancel (9 ms)'; Stopped ending shown.

checks.what: Harness error: first fixed pinned2 pass through the dll
checks.evidence: 12 invalid runs: vstest.console rejected '-nologo' when given a dll ('The argument -nologo is invalid'). No test ran; the runs were discarded and the harness fixed. Not a product result.

checks.what: Harness error: first full-suite loop
checks.command: foreach loop splatting @nb into pwsh -File eng/dotnet.ps1
checks.evidence: Runs 2-8 exited 1 within 1 s because the argument splat was malformed. No tests ran. Run 1 (with build) was green, and a direct re-run with explicit arguments passed 301 of 301. The loop was rewritten, then gave 8 of 8 green.

checks.what: Design case 2's exact load: 32 busy-loop jobs on 16 logical CPUs
checks.evidence: The machine rules cap load at half the logical processors (8). Pinned 2-CPU contention was used instead; it reproduced the flake 13 of 13 on the unfixed guard.

checks.what: Full suite under concentrated (pinned2) contention
checks.evidence: Every dotnet test start on 2 contended CPUs takes 40-70 s; a full suite would overrun a few-minute loaded pass. Full-suite load coverage is spread8 only, which does not reproduce the flake on the unfixed guard.

checks.what: Mutants of the tree's own tests for O-026/O-027 (Dispose without Drain; MaxAttemptsInKernel=1000)
checks.evidence: Code review ran them: the existing tests stayed green. I read the tree instead: no commit after 5654d9b, and neither test changed.

criteria.criterion: (slice) The flake is removed by a fix or a quarantine
criteria.how: A fix, not a quarantine: CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel is unchanged and not skipped. Under the same pinned 2-CPU contention it was red 13 of 13 on the unfixed guard and green 30 of 30 on the fix.

criteria.criterion: (slice) Repeated class and full-suite runs no longer go red (was about 3 of 50 class runs, 1 of 2 full-suite runs)
criteria.how: The 'still blocked 2 s after Cancel' failure was absent from every run: 0 of 30 class runs under pinned2, 10 of 10 full suite idle, 8 of 8 full suite under 8 busy loops. Caveat: under pinned2, 2 of 30 class runs went red on a different, pre-existing bar (CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel, 250 ms Cancel(): 355 and 717 ms). The unfixed baseline also fails that bar (1 of 6), and the build filed it as a separate defect.

criteria.criterion: (slice) An answer to whether local cancel can really exceed 2 s under load
criteria.how: Recorded at SynchronousIoCancel.cs:39-44 and in the build record: a delivered cancel does not (spike: max 622 ms), a lost cancel does, without bound (that was the flake). My runs add one thing. With the worker's CPU contended (pinned2), a call that re-blocks 3 times took up to about 2 s in total, and 8 times up to 5.1 s, although every cancel landed. So the total for a call that blocks repeatedly can approach 2 s under concentrated load.

criteria.criterion: 1. Cancel a guarded call that blocks again: worker re-blocks before the first CancelSynchronousIo returns (one CPU, worker Highest)
criteria.how: Acceptance command exit 0 (1 + 10 idle), and 30 of 30 under pinned2. The same tests are red 3 of 3 on the pre-fix guard. The trace shows each held attempt freed by the next one.

criteria.criterion: 2. The existing class test, 30 runs under heavy load
criteria.how: 30 of 30 under pinned2 contention (4 spinners plus the test process on 2 CPUs), a load shown to fail the unfixed guard 13 of 13. The design's literal 32-job load was not run: machine rules cap load at 8 CPUs.

criteria.criterion: 3. Single-wait cancel with the first attempt on a newly started thread, under load: stays well inside 2 s
criteria.how: CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel's 2 s Join held 30 of 30 under pinned2, and the longest test took 1589 ms including 200 ms of settle. The test itself went red twice, on its 250 ms Cancel() bar (a pre-existing defect).

criteria.criterion: 4. Cancel before the worker is in a synchronous call (FALSE/1168 ignored, resend lands)
criteria.how: CancelIsResentUntilACallThatHadNotReachedTheKernelIsInterrupted passed 30 of 30 under pinned2, plus every idle and full-suite run.

criteria.criterion: 5. Exit with no cancel: hot path lock-free, no attempts
criteria.how: Leave() is a single Interlocked.Exchange that returns before Drain unless the state was CancelIssued (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:287-293). ExitWithNoCancelMakesNoAttemptAndWaitsForNone passed 30 of 30 under load and in every suite run.

criteria.criterion: 6. Exit after a cancel with an attempt still in CancelSynchronousIo: waits, does not hang
criteria.how: The trace shows leave, then the held attempts' returns, then exit-returned (for example leave 490.19 ms, returns at 506 and 541 ms, exit at 541.29). AttemptsLiveAtLastDrain was 2 in every repro run. No blame-hang 60 s dump in any run.

criteria.criterion: 7. Synchronous I/O after Exit is not aborted
criteria.how: The listing and the 300 ms pending pipe wait after Exit passed in every repro and ExitWaits run (30 of 30 under load). The trace shows 0 calls after the final Leave and 0 returns after Exit.

criteria.criterion: 8. Dispose while still Cancelling with no prior Exit: handle closed only after in-flight attempts drain
criteria.how: Scratch probe with an attempt really in flight: the handle closed after the attempt returned (liveAtLastDrain=1), 3 of 3. The skip-drain mutant closed the handle first and the attempt hit it closed, 3 of 3. The tree's own test, DisposeWithoutExitWhileCancellingEndsEveryAttemptFirst, passes but cannot detect this (O-026, still open).

criteria.criterion: 9. Full suite with the repro included (affinity and priority serialized and restored)
criteria.how: 10 of 10 idle and 8 of 8 under 8 busy loops, 301 tests each, no hang. The repro class is in a DisableParallelization collection and asserts the affinity is restored.
Scratch probe holding every attempt for 1 s: peak 4 and 4 attempts, never more, 7 of 7 idle and loaded. No test in the tree pins this (O-027, still open).

criteria.criterion: 11. Delivered cancel latency over 2 s under load (non-material; answer recorded)
criteria.how: The answer is in the comment at SynchronousIoCancel.cs:39-44. In my loaded runs no single-wait cancel missed its 2 s Join (30 of 30).

criteria.criterion: 12. Thread.Start throws (non-material; slot returned, retried next tick)
criteria.how: Scratch seam threw OutOfMemoryException on the first 2 dispatches: peak stayed 1, a later tick delivered the cancel, and the drain ended. 7 of 7.

obligations.evidence: Instrumented trace in 13 idle and 6 pinned2 runs, 3 and 8 waits. Every time the worker re-blocked, the previous attempt stayed inside CancelSynchronousIo past wait-enter k+1, and returned TRUE only after attempt k+1, on another thread, had freed wait k+1 (2 of 2 and 7 of 7 per trace). Example: csio-call 1 at 222.66 ms, wait-enter 2 at 223.37, csio-call 2 at 250.10, wait-left 2 at 250.16, csio-ret-TRUE 1 at 250.26. The acceptance test that settles this is green 11 of 11 idle and 30 of 30 loaded, and red 3 of 3 on the pre-fix guard.

In every trace each attempt returned (calls = returns). Each held attempt returned once the wait it was held on had been cancelled, and the last ones after the worker left, all before Exit returned (for example leave 490.19 ms, returns 506 and 541 ms, exit 541.29). No drain hung in any run under blame-hang 60 s, idle or loaded. Measured on Windows 11 26200 only.

Trace: 0 CancelSynchronousIo calls after the final Leave and 0 returns after Exit, in 19 traces. The post-Exit 300 ms pending pipe wait was never aborted: repro 30 of 30 loaded and 11 idle, ExitWaitsForAttemptsAboutToCancelSoNoneLandsAfterIt 30 of 30 loaded. Build and code review showed with a mutant that ExitWaits fails when Drain does not wait.

Owed to build-slice and not done: HEAD is still 5654d9b and DisposeWithoutExitWhileCancellingEndsEveryAttemptFirst is unchanged. My scratch probe built the way O-026 asks (attempt held 150 ms, AttemptsLiveAtLastDrain >= 1, no CancelSynchronousIo after the handle closes) passes on the fix 3 of 3 and fails 3 of 3 with Dispose's Drain skipped. The behaviour is right; the tree's test still cannot fail on it.

Owed to build-slice and not done: ExitWaitsForAttemptsAboutToCancelSoNoneLandsAfterIt still asserts nothing about PeakAttemptsInKernel (read in git diff 1922131..5654d9b). My scratch probe shows the cap works: with all attempts held for 1 s, peak 4 and 4 attempts, 7 of 7. No test in the tree pins it.

not_reached: The design's own load for case 2 (32 busy-loop jobs on 16 logical CPUs) was not run: the machine rules cap load at 8 logical CPUs. The substitute was contention confined to CPUs 14-15. It discriminates (unfixed 13 of 13 red), but it is not the design's shape.
A full suite under concentrated contention was not run. Full-suite load coverage is 8 unpinned busy loops only, which does not reproduce the flake even on the unfixed guard.

Windows 10 was not tested. The held-in-kernel behaviour of CancelSynchronousIo, which the whole fix rests on and which contradicts Microsoft's documented remarks, was measured only on Windows 11 26200.
No real slow SMB share or cloud provider whose redirector ignores cancel was used. The cap of 4 and the unbounded drain were exercised only through the BeforeCancelCall seam and local named pipes.

The acceptance test's 2 s bar has little margin when its one pinned CPU is contended. Under pinned2 its printed Cancel-to-leave reached 1780-2051 ms in several runs (the clock is read after left.Wait returns; still 30 of 30 green). It could itself become a load flake on a machine busier on CPU 0.

The pre-existing 250 ms Cancel() bar in CancelInterruptsACallBlockedInTheKernel still goes red under concentrated contention: 2 of 30 fixed, 1 of 6 baseline. Whether that is SL-055's or a separate slice is the design's open question, which no person has answered.

Production Exit and Dispose drain with no watchdog. No hang was seen here, but a redirector that holds CancelSynchronousIo after the scan thread has left all I/O was never observed or ruled out on real network or cloud storage.
